name: Learn simple leatherworking
blurb: A card holder or a belt teaches the whole vocabulary: cutting, edge finishing, saddle stitching and hardware. Hand-stitched leather is stronger than machine-stitched.
gear: A cutting mat, a sharp knife, a stitching chisel
Waxed thread and two harness needles
steps: Learn to cut accurately with a very sharp knife against a steel rule, in one confident pass rather than several timid ones.
Learn the saddle stitch: two needles, one thread, passing through each hole from both sides. It is what makes hand-stitching outlast machine work.
Learn to mark and punch stitching holes evenly with a chisel and a mallet.
Learn edge finishing: bevel the edge, wet it, then burnish with a slicker until it is glassy. This step is what makes work look professional.
Make a simple card holder as a first project, then a belt or a knife sheath.
Learn basic hardware: rivets, snaps and buckles.
tips: Edge finishing is 80% of the perceived quality. Do not skip it.
Measure and mark everything before cutting — leather does not forgive an error the way fabric does.
proof: A hand-stitched item with even stitches and burnished edges that you would use daily.
